metadata.description: Nutrition knowledge base for condition-aware Indian vegetarian recipe generation

diabetes.label: Diabetes
diabetes.core_principle: Keep blood sugar stable. Prioritise low-GI foods, high fibre, adequate protein at every meal. Avoid refined carbs, added sugar, and fruit juices.

avoid: sugar and jaggery in large amounts
prefer: millets (bajra, jowar, ragi, foxtail)
brown rice or hand-pounded rice in small portions
whole wheat roti over maida
dal and legumes at every meal for protein and fibre
non-starchy vegetables (spinach, methi, karela, lauki)
karela (bitter gourd) — natural blood sugar regulator
fenugreek seeds (methi dana) — improves insulin sensitivity
cinnamon — add to chai or khichdi
amla — excellent for blood sugar regulation
nuts and seeds as snacks
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Fill half the plate with vegetables, quarter with protein (dal/legumes), quarter with complex carbs (millet/brown rice). Never skip meals.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: 3 main meals + 2 small snacks. No gaps longer than 3-4 hours. Avoid eating carbs alone.

condition_specific_swaps.reason: Lower GI, won't spike blood sugar

condition_specific_swaps.to: raw banana or yam (suran) in small portions
whole fruit with peel where possible

pcos.label: PCOS
pcos.core_principle: PCOS is driven by insulin resistance and hormonal imbalance. Low-GI, anti-inflammatory, high-fibre, high-protein diet is key. Avoid refined carbs, dairy in excess, and processed foods.

avoid: excess dairy (especially full-fat milk in large quantities)
soy in excess (phytoestrogens can disrupt hormones)
prefer: millets — bajra, jowar, ragi (anti-inflammatory, low GI)
lentils and legumes for plant protein
flaxseed — supports estrogen balance
pumpkin seeds — zinc for hormone health
spearmint (pudina) — reduces androgen levels
turmeric — anti-inflammatory
cinnamon — improves insulin sensitivity
leafy greens — methi, palak, sarson
berries and amla — antioxidants
healthy fats — ghee, coconut oil, nuts in moderation
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Protein at every meal. Never eat carbs alone. Include healthy fat with each meal to slow glucose absorption.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: Regular meals, never skip breakfast. Intermittent fasting should be approached carefully with PCOS.

condition_specific_swaps.from: full fat milk in large amounts
condition_specific_swaps.to: almond milk or small amount of A2 cow milk
date and nut ladoo in moderation
spearmint tea or cinnamon chai without sugar
condition_specific_swaps.reason: Spearmint reduces androgens, cinnamon helps insulin

hypertension.label: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
hypertension.core_principle: Reduce sodium, increase potassium and magnesium. DASH diet principles adapted for the Indian vegetarian kitchen. Avoid pickles, papads, packaged snacks.

avoid: excess salt — limit to 1 tsp per day total
prefer: banana — high potassium
coconut water — natural electrolyte balance
leafy greens — palak, methi (magnesium)
dal and legumes — potassium and fibre
flaxseed — omega-3, reduces BP
garlic — natural ACE inhibitor
amla — vitamin C, reduces arterial stiffness
watermelon — L-citrulline for BP
beets (chukandar) — nitrates that relax blood vessels
sesame seeds (til) — magnesium and calcium
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Low sodium across all meals. Read every label for hidden sodium. Increase potassium-rich foods at every meal.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: Regular meals. Avoid heavy dinners late at night.

condition_specific_swaps.to: fresh coriander chutney (no salt) or plain dahi

high_cholesterol.label: High Cholesterol
high_cholesterol.core_principle: Reduce saturated and trans fats. Increase soluble fibre, omega-3 fatty acids, and plant sterols. Avoid vanaspati, excess ghee, and fried foods.

avoid: packaged biscuits with partially hydrogenated oils
cream and malai in large amounts
prefer: oats — beta-glucan reduces LDL
rajma, chana, moong — soluble fibre
flaxseed — omega-3, reduces triglycerides
walnuts — best plant source of omega-3
methi seeds — lowers LDL
garlic — reduces total cholesterol
amla — antioxidant, raises HDL
eggplant (baingan) — plant sterols
okra (bhindi) — soluble fibre
olive oil or mustard oil over refined oil
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Use 1 tsp oil per serving. Include soluble fibre at every meal. One handful of nuts daily.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: Regular meals. Include oats at breakfast for maximum beta-glucan benefit.

condition_specific_swaps.to: cold-pressed mustard oil or olive oil
1 tsp ghee max + mustard oil for cooking

thyroid.label: Thyroid (Hypothyroidism)
thyroid.core_principle: Support thyroid function with selenium, iodine, and zinc. Avoid goitrogens in raw form (cruciferous vegetables). Time nutrients around medication.

avoid: raw cruciferous vegetables in large amounts — raw cabbage, raw cauliflower, raw broccoli (cooking neutralises goitrogens)
excess soy — inhibits thyroid hormone absorption
excess millet in hypothyroidism (goitrogenic in very large amounts)
coffee within 1 hour of thyroid medication
calcium-rich foods within 4 hours of medication
prefer: iodised salt — essential for thyroid hormone production
selenium-rich foods — Brazil nuts (1-2/day), sunflower seeds
zinc sources — pumpkin seeds, chickpeas, cashews
cooked cruciferous vegetables are fine — cooking destroys goitrogens
turmeric — anti-inflammatory
ginger — supports metabolism
coconut oil — medium-chain fatty acids support thyroid
whole grains — energy for sluggish metabolism
iron-rich foods — spinach, lentils (iron deficiency worsens hypothyroidism)
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Balanced meals. Eat cruciferous vegetables cooked, not raw. Take thyroid medication on empty stomach, wait 1 hour before eating.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: Medication timing is critical. Consistent meal times support metabolic rhythm.

condition_specific_swaps.to: rotate with whole wheat and brown rice

condition_specific_swaps.reason: Iodine essential for thyroid hormone production

condition_specific_swaps.from: raw smoothies with kale/spinach in excess

obesity.label: Obesity / Weight Management
obesity.core_principle: Create sustainable calorie deficit without hunger. High fibre, high protein, low refined carbs. Focus on satiety and habit change, not crash dieting.

avoid: refined carbs — maida, white rice, white bread
liquid calories — juice, chai with sugar, lassi with sugar
prefer: high-volume, low-calorie foods — salads, soups, sabzi
protein at every meal — dal, legumes, paneer, curd
fibre-rich foods — vegetables, whole grains, flaxseed
water before meals — reduces appetite
green tea — mild metabolism boost
millets — filling, lower calorie density than rice
sprouts — high protein, low calorie
buttermilk (chaas) over full-fat lassi
roasted makhana, chana over fried snacks
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Use smaller plates. Half plate vegetables, quarter protein, quarter complex carbs. Chew slowly. Stop at 80% full.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: No eating after 8pm. Largest meal at lunch, lightest at dinner. 12-hour overnight fast minimum.

condition_specific_swaps.to: low-fat dahi or hung curd for raita
plain chaas with jeera and mint
cauliflower rice or small portion brown rice
roasted makhana, chana, or sprouts chaat
dal with minimal ghee, extra haldi and jeera

condition_specific_swaps.reason: Natural sweetness with fibre and healthy fat

general_wellbeing.label: General Wellbeing & Weight Management
general_wellbeing.core_principle: No specific condition — just eating well, feeling good, and maintaining a healthy weight. Focus on whole foods, balanced macros, gut health, and sustainable habits rooted in the Indian kitchen.

avoid: excess sodium from pickles, papads, packaged masalas
seed oils high in omega-6 (refined sunflower, soybean oil)
eating out of boredom or stress
prefer: whole grains and millets as carb base
dal or legumes at every meal for plant protein
rainbow vegetables — eat across colours daily
fermented foods daily — dahi, idli, dosa, kanji for gut health
seasonal and local produce over imported superfoods
adequate hydration — 8-10 glasses water + coconut water, chaas
healthy fats — 1 tsp ghee, cold-pressed oils, nuts and seeds
home-cooked meals over restaurant or packaged food
mindful eating — no screens, chew slowly
dietary_rules.portion_guidance: Balanced thali approach — dal + sabzi + roti/rice + dahi. No food group is off-limits. Moderation over restriction.
dietary_rules.meal_timing: 3 balanced meals. Avoid eating after 8pm. Light dinner. One optional small snack if needed.

condition_specific_swaps.to: oats with nuts and seeds or ragi porridge
condition_specific_swaps.reason: Whole food, no hidden sugar or additives

condition_specific_swaps.to: skip sugar or use 1 small date
condition_specific_swaps.reason: Reduce daily sugar load without feeling deprived

condition_specific_swaps.to: roasted chana, makhana, or sprouts chaat
condition_specific_swaps.reason: Real food, more nutrients, less sodium
Fewer hidden calories, more control over ingredients

condition_specific_swaps.to: simple moong dal chilla or dahi with fruit

what_to_check: Serving size — companies make it tiny to hide how much you're actually eating
Added sugar — look for it under 20+ names: dextrose, corn syrup, maltose, fructose
Sodium — anything above 600mg per 100g is high
Ingredients list — if it has more than 5-6 ingredients or ones you can't pronounce, reconsider
Trans fat — '0g trans fat' can still mean up to 0.49g per serving. Check for 'partially hydrogenated oils'
Protein — most Indian packaged snacks have less than 2g. Not a protein source.
Fibre — aim for at least 3g per serving in any grain product
red_flags_in_indian_packaged_foods: 'Multigrain' doesn't mean whole grain — check if refined flour is first ingredient
'No added sugar' may still contain fruit concentrates or artificial sweeteners
'Baked not fried' can still be high in refined flour and sodium
'Natural flavours' is a catch-all term — means nothing specific
Health claims on front of pack are marketing — always flip to the nutrition label

diabetic_day.lunch: 2 jowar roti + palak dal + karela sabzi + plain dahi
diabetic_day.dinner: Foxtail millet khichdi with lots of vegetables + chaas

pcos_day.mid_morning: 1 tbsp flaxseed in water or smoothie
pcos_day.lunch: 2 bajra roti + chana dal + methi sabzi + dahi
pcos_day.dinner: Moong dal soup + sautéed vegetables + small bowl brown rice

hypertension_day.lunch: 2 whole wheat roti + toor dal (no extra salt) + lauki sabzi + dahi
hypertension_day.dinner: Dal khichdi + palak sabzi + chaas (no salt)
